operators.name: cat_maximum_forward
semantics: Corresponds to reference statement x1 = torch.cat((x, x), dim=1). The op concatenates the input tensor with itself along dimension 1, doubling the channel dimension from 3 to 6. Input is expected to be float32 CUDA with shape [16, 3, 2048, 2048]. Output is float32 CUDA with shape [16, 6, 2048, 2048].

Then applies torch.maximum(x1, x1) elementwise. Since both operands are identical, this simply copies x1 to x2. The output is the same as the concatenated tensor, so the op ultimately returns a tensor identical to torch.cat((x, x), dim=1). The maximum operation involves no broadcasting because the shapes match exactly.

The op must operate on CUDA tensors, using a grid-stride loop to handle the large number of elements (402,653,184) and must write every output element. The output tensor must be allocated on the current CUDA stream and have the same dtype as input.
No bias or other parameters. The return is a plain tensor, not a named tuple.

Concatenate input tensor x with itself along dimension 1 (channels). Given input shape [16, 3, 2048, 2048], output shape is [16, 6, 2048, 2048]. Data type is torch.float32, device CUDA. No broadcasting; the operation simply copies x twice into the channel dimension.

Elementwise maximum of x1 with itself. Since both operands are identical, the result equals x1. Shape remains [16, 6, 2048, 2048], dtype float32, device CUDA. No broadcasting because shapes match. The result is a new tensor (not a view) but identical in values.
Return the tensor x2. Shape [16, 6, 2048, 2048], dtype float32, device CUDA. This is the final output of the model.
